about: How equipment schedules are read off the drawing sheets (build step 4). Header words are compared after squashing spaces, ignoring case and a trailing full stop or colon. Patterns are regular expressions, matched ignoring case. Extend this file, never the code.
tag_header_pattern_about: A key-column header the exact list above misses ("UNIT", "AC UNIT", "PUMP NO.", "FAN NO.", "AC UNIT NO."), matched on the squashed upper-case header with its trailing stop taken off. A column so headed is the tag column only when most of its cells below are unit tags (READ-5).
quantity_headers_about: A column that counts the units a row stands for. A row whose tag is a type takes its quantity from it (header compared whole: NO. OF PORTS is not one).
schedule_heading_about: A line of a sheet's text that heads a schedule ("EXHAUST FAN SCHEDULE", "ROOFTOP UNIT SCHEDULE (1 OF 2)"). When a schedule sheet's tables can't be read (a picture read by OCR), its units are counted from its text, each under the nearest heading above it.
type_list_titles_about: A schedule with one of these words in its title lists types of air device, silencer or fixture (passive items no controller serves), not units: a tag column whose prefix isn't in equipment.json is read as types there, never counted as units.
air_device_words_about: Words that say a schedule lists passive air devices (diffusers, registers, grilles, louvers, air outlets, silencers) by type: in its title, its basis-of-design line, a band row of its key column, or most of its description cells. Such a schedule's codes (B1, CD, LRD-A) are never units or controls systems, whatever their prefix (READ-3).
